775-when-the-sleeper-wakes.description: A book by Herbert George Wells. “That is what I have tried. I have followed the coast, day after day--from New Quay. It has only added muscular fatigue to the mental. The cause of this unrest was overwork--trouble. There was something--”

arxiv-2106-07944.title: Simplifying Robot Programming using Augmented Reality and End-User Development
arxiv-2106-07944.creator: Enes Yigitbas, Ivan Jovanovikj, Gregor Engels
arxiv-2106-07944.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Enes Yigitbas, Ivan Jovanovikj, Gregor Engels. Robots are widespread across diverse application contexts. Teaching robots to perform tasks, in their respective contexts, demands a high domain and programming expertise. However, robot programming faces high entry barriers due to the complexity of robot programming itself. Even for experts robot programming is a cumbersome and error-prone task where faulty robot programs can be created, causing damage when being executed on a real robot.

arxiv-2211-10190.title: Weyl groupoids and superalgebraic sets.
arxiv-2211-10190.creator: Ian M. Musson
arxiv-2211-10190.description: Abstract This paper is a contribution to the study of the geometry of algebras related the Weyl groupoid initiated in [ 9 ] . The Nullstellensatz gives a bijection between radical ideals of such an algebra and their zero loci, the superalgebraic sets.

arxiv-2212-14081.title: Quantum Reference Frames for Lorentz Symmetry
arxiv-2212-14081.creator: Luca Apadula, Esteban Castro-Ruiz, C ˇ \check{\text{C}} aslav Brukner
arxiv-2212-14081.description: Abstract Since their first introduction, Quantum Reference Frame (QRF) transformations have been extensively discussed, generalising the covariance of physical laws to the quantum domain. Despite important progress, a formulation of QRF transformations for Lorentz symmetry is still lacking. The present work aims to fill this gap.

arxiv-2301-07754.title: Charged magnons on the surface of a topological Insulator
arxiv-2301-07754.creator: I. Martinez-Berumen, W. A. Coish, T. Pereg-Barnea
arxiv-2301-07754.description: Abstract We study a system of two-dimensional Dirac electrons (as is realized on the surface of a 3D topological insulator) coupled to an array of localized spins. The spins are coupled ferromagnetically to each other, forming an ordered ground state with low-energy spin-wave excitations (magnons). The Dirac electrons couple to the spins through a spin-dependent effective Zeeman field.

arxiv-2306-02101.title: Fate of bubble clusters rising in a quiescent liquid
arxiv-2306-02101.creator: Tian Ma 1, ∗,, Hendrik Hessenkemper 1, ∗,, Dirk Lucas 1, Andrew D. Bragg 2
arxiv-2306-02101.description: Abstract We use experiments to study the evolution of bubble clusters in a swarm of freely rising, deformable bubbles. A new machine learning-aided algorithm allows us to identify and track bubbles in clusters and measure the cluster lifetimes. The results indicate that contamination in the carrier liquid can enhance the formation of bubble clusters and prolong the cluster lifetimes.

arxiv-2404-05750.title: K-theories and Free Inductive Graded Rings in Abstract Quadratic Forms Theories
arxiv-2404-05750.creator: Kaique Matias de Andrade Roberto
arxiv-2404-05750.description: Abstract We build on previous work on multirings ( [ 3 ] ) that provides generalizations of the available abstract quadratic forms theories (special groups and real semigroups) to the context of multirings ( [ 17 ] , [ 7 ] ).

arxiv-2407-12421.title: SafePowerGraph: Safety-aware Evaluation of Graph Neural Networks for Transmission Power Grids Thanks: LIST: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology
arxiv-2407-12421.creator: Salah GHAMIZI, Aleksandar BOJCHEVSKI, Aoxiang MA, Jun CAO
arxiv-2407-12421.description: Abstract Power grids are critical infrastructures of paramount importance to modern society and their rapid evolution and interconnections has heightened the complexity of power systems (PS) operations. Traditional methods for grid analysis struggle with the computational demands of large-scale RES and ES integration, prompting the adoption of machine learning (ML) techniques, particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).

arxiv-2412-10234.title: Iterated integrals and cohomology
arxiv-2412-10234.creator: Kathrin Bringmann, Nikolaos Diamantis
arxiv-2412-10234.description: Abstract . We introduce an extension of the standard cohomology which is characterised by maps that fail to be classical cocycles by products of simpler maps. The construction is motivated by the study of Manin’s noncommutative modular symbols and of false theta functions.

arxiv-2503-01680.title: Numerical invariants for weighted cscK metrics
arxiv-2503-01680.creator: Thibaut Delcroix, Simon Jubert
arxiv-2503-01680.description: Abstract . In K-stability, the delta invariant of a Fano variety encodes the existence of Kähler-Einstein metrics. We introduce a weighted analytic delta invariant, and a reduced version, that characterize the existence of weighted solitons. We further prove a sufficient condition of existence of weighted cscK metrics in terms of this invariant.

arxiv-2509-09602.title: LAVA: Language Model Assisted Verbal Autopsy for Cause-of-Death Determination
arxiv-2509-09602.creator: Yiqun T. Chen, Tyler H. McCormick, Li Liu, Abhirup Datta
arxiv-2509-09602.description: Abstract Verbal autopsy (VA) is a critical tool for estimating causes of death in resource-limited settings where medical certification is unavailable. This study presents LA-VA, a proof-of-concept pipeline that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with traditional algorithmic approaches and embedding-based classification for improved cause-of-death prediction.

arxiv-2512-19092.title: A Large Language Model Based Method for Complex Logical Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2512-19092.creator: Ziyan Zhang, Chao Wang, Zhuo Chen, Lei Chen, Chiyi Li, Kai Song
arxiv-2512-19092.description: Abstract Reasoning over knowledge graphs (KGs) with first-order logic (FOL) queries is challenging due to the inherent incompleteness of real-world KGs and the compositional complexity of logical query structures. Most existing methods rely on embedding entities and relations into continuous geometric spaces and answer queries via differentiable set operations.

pmc-10642058.title: Study methodology and insights from the palovarotene clinical development program in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
pmc-10642058.creator: Robert J. Pignolo, Mona Al Mukaddam, Geneviève Baujat, Matthew A. Brown, Carmen De Cunto, Edward C. Hsiao, Richard Keen, Kim-Hanh Le Quan Sang, Donna R. Grogan, Rose Marino, Andrew R. Strahs, Frederick S. Kaplan
pmc-10642058.description: BackgroundThe design of clinical trials in rare diseases is often complicated by a lack of real-world translational knowledge. Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder characterized by skeletal malformations and progressive heterotopic ossification (HO). Palovarotene is a selective retinoic acid receptor gamma agonist.

pmc-11603799.title: Educational design insights for interprofessional immersive simulation to prepare allied health students for clinical placements
pmc-11603799.creator: Jennie Brentnall, Laura Rossiter, Belinda Judd, Emma Cowley, Keith McCormick, Ruth Turk, Debbie Thackray
pmc-11603799.description: BackgroundPositive outcomes of simulation programmes to prepare students for placement are widely noted. However, few studies adequately describe considerations for designing allied health placement simulations. There exists a conceptual framework to guide such simulation design, which draws on theory and educational expertise but to date lacks varied stakeholder perspectives.

pmc-11641960.title: Effects of Acute Maximum-Intensity Exercise on Matrix Metalloproteinase-2, -9, and Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-1 Levels in Adult Males with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Treated with Insulin Pumps
pmc-11641960.creator: Joanna Kryst, Bartłomiej Matejko, Olga Czerwińska-Ledwig, Łukasz Tota, Roxana Zuziak, Anna Piotrowska, Alessandro Delitala
pmc-11641960.description: Background: Dysregulation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) activity is considered one of the potential causes of vascular complications in diabetic patients. Since training volume may influence MMPs levels in varying ways, the aim of our study was to evaluate changes in MMPs levels following acute maximum-intensity exercise in male patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

pmc-12431290.title: Optimizing Deep Learning-Based Crack Detection Using No-Reference Image Quality Assessment in a Mobile Tunnel Scanning System
pmc-12431290.creator: Chulhee Lee, Donggyou Kim, Dongku Kim
pmc-12431290.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The mobile tunnel scanning system (MTSS) enables efficient tunnel inspection; however, motion blur (MB) generated at high travel speeds remains a major factor undermining the reliability of deep-learning-based crack detection. This study focuses on investigating how horizontally oriented MB in MTSS imagery affects the crack-detection performance of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and proposes a data-centric quality-assurance framework that leverages no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) to optimize model performance.

pmc-13019994.title: Effect of ultrasonic treatment on structure and physicochemical properties of starch: An updated review
pmc-13019994.creator: Ning Bei, Zihao Song, Yuqi Shen, Guanhua Liu, Fang Dong, Xia Liu
pmc-13019994.description: Graphical abstract Introduction Starch is a naturally abundant, low-cost, and renewable high-molecular-weight polysaccharide. As the main energy reserve of many plants, it is widely distributed in cereals, legumes, and tuber crops. It also serves as a foundation of dietary energy for billions of people worldwide and accounts for approximately two-thirds of daily caloric intake.

pmc-13385334.title: Gut microbiota in health and disease
pmc-13385334.creator: Yangziyi Li, Xueyan Xiao, Xin Jiang, Xinyi Li, Weijun Wang, Rong Lin
pmc-13385334.description: The gut microbiota is integral to host physiology, contributing to metabolic homeostasis, epithelial barrier integrity, immune balance, and bidirectional communication along gut–organ axes. Disruption of this ecosystem, commonly referred to as dysbiosis, is increasingly implicated in a wide range of gastrointestinal and extra-intestinal diseases.
